b1-n-loch: There is a small opening in your sock and your toe is sticking out.
Workers dig a deep one in the road to repair a pipe.
A golfer hits the ball into the small round one on the green.
b1-n-vorbereitung: Before the party, you buy food, clean the flat and put up decorations. What noun describes all the work you do before the event?
Before a long trip, you pack your bags, check your tickets and book a hotel.
You study every evening for next month's exam. This is the work you do to get ready.
b1-v-tauchen: At the seaside, you put on a mask and go underwater to look at colourful fish.
You hold your breath and go under the water in the swimming pool to pick up a coin from the bottom.
You quickly put your biscuit into your tea for a second and take it out again.
b1-n-herz: After running, you put your hand on your chest and feel it beating fast.
On Valentine's Day, you draw a red shape on a card for the person you love.
The doctor listens to your chest with a stethoscope to check the organ that pumps your blood.
b1-adj-bloss: In summer, the child walks across the grass with nothing on her feet. Which adjective describes her feet?
Just the idea of the exam makes you nervous, even before you have seen any question. It is only the idea, nothing more.
He lies on the beach with his arms and legs not covered by any clothes at all.
b1-n-sosse: With your pasta, the cook pours a red tomato mixture on top.
At a fast-food restaurant, you ask for ketchup or mayonnaise to dip your chips in.
At Sunday dinner, a warm brown liquid is poured over the roast meat. What is it called?
b1-v-beantragen: You want to travel to another country and need a new passport, so you fill in a form at the office and hand it in.
A student asks the university for financial help and sends in a formal request.
You write to your boss and officially ask for two weeks of holiday.
b1-n-boden: You drop a glass and it falls onto the surface of the room that you walk on.
Farmers check the earth in their field to see if plants can grow well in it.
At the deep end of the pool you can see the lowest part, covered with blue tiles.
b1-n-wahl: On Sunday, citizens put a paper into a box to choose a new mayor.
In the restaurant you have to decide between fish and meat. You can pick from the options.
The shop offers the same shirt in five colours, so you can make a decision which to take.
b1-v-foerdern: Parents buy books and music lessons to help their talented child grow.
A company gives money to young artists to help them start their careers.
A teacher gives the quiet pupil more chances so that he improves.
b1-adj-schuldig: In court, the jury says that the accused man really committed the crime. Which adjective describes him?
Your dog ate the cake and now looks away with a bad conscience. It knows it did it.
A boy broke the window with his ball and says: 'It was my fault.'
b1-n-werk: A great composer's famous piece of music, like a symphony, is part of what he created in his life.
A big car company has a large industrial site where thousands of people build cars.
A museum shows all the paintings and drawings by one artist. We call them what he created.
b1-adv-trotzdem: It is raining hard, but you go for a run anyway. Which adverb means 'despite that'?
You are sick, but you go to work. Which word means 'still'?
The test was very hard. Even so, you got a good mark.
b1-n-semester: At university, the lectures are divided into two parts of the year. A student says he is in his third one.
The winter lectures go from October to March. What is this period called?
A student pays a fee every half year to be enrolled.
b1-n-fortschritt: After months of practice, your German is much better than in January. What have you made?
A teacher tells a pupil: 'You have improved a lot this month. Keep going!'
A scientist finds a new way to cure a disease. It is a big step forward for humanity.
b1-v-klettern: A child goes up the tree in the garden using the branches.
At a sports hall, people use hands and feet to go up a wall with colourful holds.
Hikers go up a steep rock using ropes.
b1-n-krokodil: In a river in Africa, a big green reptile with sharp teeth lies still in the water.
A boy has a toy: a green animal with a very long mouth and many teeth.
In the story of Peter Pan, a big green animal swallowed a clock and goes tick-tock.
b1-adj-interessiert: You listen carefully to the talk and ask many questions because you want to know more.
A student says he is keen to learn more about history.
Which adjective describes a person who wants to find out more about a topic?
b1-n-jugend: Your grandfather says: 'In my early years, we had no phones.' He talks about the time when he was young.
The town opens a club where teenagers can meet, play sports and make music.
A news article says: 'Many young people today use social media.' Which noun covers young people as a group?
b1-v-zurechtkommen: You moved abroad and can handle daily life alone without much help.
Two roommates have very different habits, but they get along well.
Your boss asks: 'Do you manage with the new software, or do you need help?'
b1-n-haustier: Your child asks for a small animal like a cat or a rabbit to keep at home.
The hotel sign asks: 'Is your dog or cat with you?' It means animals that live with a family.
You buy food for the animals that live in your home as companions.
b1-n-kritik: The newspaper writes about a new film and says what is good and bad about it.
Your boss says: 'This report has several problems.' He judges your work in a negative way.
A pupil says he cannot stand it when others point out his faults.
b1-v-hupen: The light turns green, but the car in front of you does not move. The driver behind you presses a button on the steering wheel and makes a loud noise.
At a wedding, the cars drive along the streets and make noise to celebrate.
A taxi driver warns a pedestrian who steps onto the road by making a short, loud sound.
b1-n-nase: You smell fresh bread through the middle of your face.
When you have a cold, you need a tissue for this part of the face.
In the story of Pinocchio, this part of the face grows when he lies.
b1-adj-ueblich: In Germany it is normal to shake hands when you meet. It is the accepted way.
The waiter asks: 'The same as always?' You say yes, the way it is regularly done.
At the shop, cheese costs the standard price. Which adjective means 'normal, as usual'?
b1-n-wanderung: On Sunday, we walk for five hours in the mountains with backpacks and good boots.
Every autumn, birds fly south in big groups. What do we call this long yearly movement?
A club organises a 20 km walk along trails and through the forest.
b1-n-schmutz: After playing football in the rain, the boys' clothes are covered in brown stuff.
The floor in the kitchen is full of dust and stains, so you must clean it.
Your boots are covered in mud after the walk.
b1-v-senden: You write an email and press a button so it goes to your friend.
A TV station shows the football match live at 8 pm.
The red light in the radio studio shows that you are on the air.
b1-adv-meinetwegen: A friend asks if he can turn up the music. You do not mind. Which adverb means 'as far as I am concerned'?
You tell a friend not to cancel the party because of you, it should not be done on your account.
'Do you care where we eat?' 'Go ahead, it is fine for me.' Which adverb means 'for my sake'?
b1-n-lehrstelle: After school, a 16-year-old looks for a job where he can learn to become a mechanic.
An ad says: 'We offer a place for a young person to learn the hairdressing trade.'
A girl sends applications to bakeries to find a spot where she can train for three years.
b1-adj-mittlerer: The company is not small and not large. It is of a size between the two.
The man is of average height, neither tall nor short.
You press the button in the centre of the three buttons.
b1-n-konsum: Experts say people buy and use too many goods, such as clothes and gadgets. They are worried about it.
A doctor warns about the amount of sugar people eat and drink every day.
The report talks about how much electricity people use in a year.
b1-v-anschaffen: Your family decides to get a dog and all the things it needs.
The office needs new computers, and the manager decides to buy them.
A couple plans to get a car because the baby is coming.
b1-n-pilz: In autumn, you walk in the forest and collect brown things with caps to cook.
On a pizza, there are slices of a white vegetable that grows in the dark.
In a fairy tale, a red one with white dots is poisonous.
b1-n-beschaeftigung: At the job centre they ask if you have work at the moment.
An elderly woman needs something to do during the day to keep busy, like reading and gardening.
On the form there is a line for your current work or activity.
b1-n-lerner: A man takes a language course and studies German in the evening.
A beginner app shows a message for the man who uses it to study new words.
A teacher talks to a man who is new to the course and calls him by the name for someone who is learning.
b1-v-aufregen: Slow customers in the queue make you angry and you cannot stay calm.
A scary film made the children very excited and nervous.
The bad news upset my mother very much.
b1-adj-rechtlich: A lawyer says there are no problems according to the law. Which adjective means 'relating to the law'?
Before signing the contract, you check if everything is correct from the point of view of the law.
The company has questions about its contract and asks its law adviser.
b1-n-vorteil: Living near work saves you time every day. It is a good thing that helps you.
A tall basketball player has this over the others.
A salesman lists why the new phone is better than the old one: more battery, better camera.
b1-n-reform: The school system will be changed for the better in a big way with new rules.
The university announces a major reorganisation of all courses to improve them.
Which noun means a big planned change to improve a system?
b1-v-dienen: An old sofa is used as a bed for guests.
A butler works for a rich lord in an old film.
This box is used as a table when you have visitors.
b1-n-bevoelkerung: A statistic says that 83 million people live in the country.
The town announces that all people living in the area should stay inside during the storm.
The city grows every year because more people live in it.
b1-adj-wunderschoen: You see a sunset over the sea with golden colours. It is extremely lovely.
The bride walks in and everybody says she looks stunning.
Your holiday was perfect, with sun, good food and nice people.
b1-n-schwiegermutter: Your husband's mother comes to visit for the weekend and cooks for you.
A woman complains: 'My husband's mother always tells me how to cook.'
At the wedding, the bride meets the groom's mother for the first time as part of the family.
b1-adv-worum: Your friend says he needs to talk to you about something. You ask what the topic is. Which question word means 'about what'?
A colleague says there will be a meeting. You ask: 'What is it about?'
Which question word do you need to ask: 'What is the book about?'
b1-v-brechen: You fall from your bike and your arm bone cracks. The doctor says you have done this to it.
You snap a chocolate bar in two pieces with your hands.
A person does not keep his promise. He does this to it.
b1-n-reaktion: You tell your friend a surprising secret. How he behaves right at that moment is important.
In the chemistry lesson, you mix two liquids and they start to bubble.
The doctor tests how your body responds to a new medicine, for example with a rash.
b1-n-schuessel: At breakfast, you pour cereal and milk into a round, deep dish.
You make salad in a large round container to put on the table.
A dog's food is placed in a round container on the floor.
b1-n-erinnerung: You look at old photos and think of your childhood holidays.
A small gift from a trip makes you think of the place, like a keepsake.
Your phone buzzes: 'Doctor tomorrow at 9.' It is a note that helps you not to forget.
b1-v-vermeiden: You take another way to work so that you do not meet your old boss.
The doctor says you should stay away from fatty food.
You do not want a fight, so you keep away from the topic of money.
b1-adj-aengstlich: A small child hides behind her mother when she sees a big dog.
A man looks nervous and pale before his dentist's appointment.
A cat trembles in a corner during a thunderstorm.
b1-n-mauer: A tall stone structure surrounds the garden and keeps strangers out.
Workers build with bricks and cement, row by row, the outer barrier of a house.
A cat sits on top of the old stone structure around the castle.
b1-n-fachmann: Your heating is broken, so you call a man who really knows the job.
You cannot fix a computer problem, so you ask a man who is a specialist.
The company hires a man with many years of experience in the field.
b1-v-beweisen: The detective shows a clear fact, a fingerprint, that shows the butler did it.
A scientist shows with an experiment that his idea is right.
You show everybody that you can do it by winning the race.
b1-n-handel: In a town, merchants buy and sell goods in big amounts. This is their business.
Two people agree on the price at the market. They have made a deal.
Countries exchange goods with each other, such as wine for cars.
b1-n-zeichen: At the crossing you see a round red board that tells you not to enter.
On the keyboard, every letter, number or @ is one of these.
A heart on a card is one of love.
b1-adj-historisch: The old town has ancient buildings from the Middle Ages. Which adjective means 'from past times'?
The first landing on the moon was a very important moment in the past.
A film is based on real events from the past.
b1-n-richter: In a courtroom, a man in a black robe decides about the case.
Your uncle works in a court and decides who is right in disputes. What is his job?
In a TV show about trials, a man says: 'Silence in the court!'
b1-v-ordnen: You put your files in the right order, by date.
You sort your books on the shelf by size.
A teacher tells students to put the cards in the correct order: first, second, third.
b1-n-girokonto: At the bank, you open an account to receive your salary and pay your bills. It is not a savings account.
Your landlord asks for the account where you pay your rent every month.
You get a debit card linked to an account to pay for everyday things.
b1-n-gegend: 'It is a beautiful part of the country with hills and lakes.'
A tourist asks if there are good restaurants in this neighbourhood.
You live in a quiet part of town.
b1-adv-gar: You stress that you have no time whatsoever. Which small word means 'at all'?
'He does not want to go there at all.' Which adverb makes 'not' stronger?
The film was not bad, it was even great. Which word means 'even' in a strong sense?
b1-v-ueberreden: Your friend does not want to come to the party, but you talk to him until he says yes.
A salesman convinces you to buy the more expensive phone.
Your children want ice cream, and they talk you into it.
b1-adj-verwandt: Your cousin and you share grandparents. You are family.
Spanish and Italian come from the same old language. They are closely linked.
At the wedding someone asks: 'Are you family?' 'Yes, I am the bride's uncle.'
b1-n-misstrauen: You do not believe your new colleague and think he lies. You feel suspicion.
After being cheated once, you no longer trust salespeople.
A detective feels something is wrong with the story. He has doubts about a person's honesty.
b1-n-ereignis: A big football match or festival happens in the city. It is something important that took place.
On the news: 'The biggest one of the year was the flood.'
Something unusual happened yesterday on your street. The police say they are looking into the incident.
b1-v-fuerchten: You are scared of spiders and would not touch one.
A child is afraid of the dark and does not want the light off.
I worry that the exam will be too hard. I dread it.
b1-n-nachwuchs: A football club trains young players who may become future stars.
A couple gets a baby, the new member of the family.
A company is missing young professionals. The next generation is needed.
b1-n-aushilfe: A shop hires a person for just two weeks at Christmas.
A student works only at weekends in a cafe as temporary help.
The restaurant's cook is ill, so they call someone temporary to help.
b1-adj-mager: A cat has visible ribs and looks very thin.
At the butcher's you ask for meat with no fat in it.
After an illness, he lost a lot of weight and looks too thin.
b1-n-zuhause: After a long trip you say there is no place like the place where you live and feel comfortable.
Your grandmother's house always feels like the place where you belong.
You call your mother and say you are coming back to the place where you live.
b1-v-stehlen: A pickpocket takes a wallet from a tourist's bag without anyone seeing.
In a shop, a teenager hides a chocolate bar in his pocket and walks out without paying.
Somebody took your bike from outside the station.
b1-n-schmuck: She wears a gold necklace, rings and earrings.
In the shop window you see rings, bracelets and chains.
Burglars took her valuables: rings and chains.
b1-n-wirtin: A woman runs the small pub in the village and serves the drinks.
A student rents a room in the house of an old woman who owns it. Who is she?
At the inn, the woman who owns the place welcomes you.
b1-v-unterbrechen: You are talking and somebody starts to speak in the middle of your sentence.
The film stops for a few minutes for ads.
A fire alarm makes the teacher stop the lesson for a while.
b1-n-kontrolle: The ticket inspector checks all passengers' tickets on the train.
At the airport, officers check your bag.
The driver loses grip on the road and cannot steer. He has lost power over the car.
b1-adj-dauernd: The neighbour's dog barks all the time, day and night, without stopping.
Your phone rings again and again without a break.
The builder says the new roof will stay for a very long time.
b1-n-liste: Before going to the supermarket, you write what you need under each other on a paper.
The teacher reads the names of all students from a sheet to check who is there.
You write down the things to do today, one under the other.
b1-adv-jeweils: Two bags of apples cost 3 euros each time. Which adverb means 'each time'?
Each of the three kids gets two sweets.
Which adverb means 'each time' or 'at a time'?
b1-n-wirtschaft: The news says that the country's production and trade are growing and unemployment is falling.
In the village there is a small traditional place where you get beer and schnitzel.
A student studies how companies and money work in a country.
b1-v-zuschauen: You stand at the side of the field and look at children playing football, without joining in.
Children watch the magician perform his tricks.
Your father cooks and you stand next to him and see how he does it.
b1-n-auftritt: A singer walks on stage and sings in front of the crowd tonight.
The band has a show in a small club on Friday.
The actor's first moment on the stage in the play.
b1-adj-verliebt: You cannot stop thinking about her, and your heart beats faster when she smiles.
A couple holds hands and looks into each other's eyes.
A girl says: 'I think I have fallen for him.'
b1-n-metropole: Tokyo and New York are huge cities with millions of people.
Berlin and Paris are big cultural capitals.
A very big city is the centre of business and culture.
b1-v-beruhigen: A crying baby is rocked by his mother until he is quiet.
The nurse tells the nervous patient not to worry and everything will be fine.
A teacher tells a noisy class to settle down.
b1-n-muttersprache: It is the language you learned first from your parents as a child.
On a form: 'Which language did you speak at home as a baby?'
A teacher says: 'Translate into the language you learned first.'
b1-n-maler: A man puts colours on a canvas in his studio and sells pictures.
A man with a brush and white paint is painting the walls of your flat.
The man who created pictures like Van Gogh did.
b1-v-verbessern: You practise every day to make your pronunciation better.
A teacher checks your homework and fixes the mistakes.
A company updates its app to make it work better.
b1-n-mehrheit: In a vote, 60 out of 100 people raise their hands for yes. The larger part decides.
Most people in the village use the bus.
The class decides by voting and the bigger group wins.
b1-adj-sparsam: She buys only what she needs and never wastes money.
The new car uses very little petrol.
A man turns off every light and does not waste anything.
b1-n-einnahme: At the end of the day, the shop owner counts the money that came in.
A cafe's income last month was 10,000 euros.
The accountant wrote down all the money the company received.
b1-n-schwiegervater: Your wife's father comes for dinner on Sunday.
At the wedding, the groom thanks the bride's father.
A man talks about his wife's father, who gave them a house.
b1-v-umdrehen: You hear your name behind you and look back, turning your body.
A cook flips the pancake in the pan.
You flip the card to see the other side.
b1-n-bedarf: A hospital needs more nurses. There is a high demand.
The company checks how much material it requires for next month.
The label says: 'Take the medicine only when you require it.'
b1-adv-hoechstens: You say you can pay at most 20 euros, not a cent more.
The class has no more than 15 students.
'How long will it take?' 'At the very most ten minutes.'
b1-adj-zuverlaessig: A friend always comes on time and keeps his promises.
An old car starts every morning without trouble.
A worker you can always count on.
b1-n-knochen: The X-ray shows that the hard white part in your arm is broken.
A dog chews a hard white thing after dinner.
A skeleton in a school classroom is made of these.
b1-v-leisten: A runner gives a great performance this season. She achieves a lot.
You say that you cannot afford a new car right now.
A worker produces a lot in one day.
b1-n-wiederholung: Before the exam, you go through old lessons once more.
The TV shows an episode again that was on last week.
The teacher says: 'Please say it again, once more.'
b1-n-enttaeuschung: You waited for weeks for the trip, but it rains the whole time. You feel sad because it was not what you hoped.
He fails the exam and feels sad and let down.
The gift was not what the child wished for.
